utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. No preliminaries were announced. Therefore, we'll wait for the witness to enter the courtroom. Yes, Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Just one small point, Your Honour. Yesterday, D1464 was admitted into evidence, and I believe it should be under seal due to the personal identifying information inside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we'll keep on the safe side --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yeah, that's fine, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, we'll keep on the safe side, and therefore D1464 is under seal and not a public exhibit any longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Radovanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Mr. Ivetic will now continue his examination. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Professor.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We left off yesterday, and I'd like to call up again but not broadcast, D1464, under seal. And if need be, I think there's still a hard copy in the possession of the usher. And now we have the English on our screens. Yesterday we talked about this column that says new ethnicity and has the value 5 which you indicated was for the Bosnian Muslims. Whose ethnicity is it that is being reflected in this column? Which of the two individuals in each -- which of the two individuals, one under the ICRC and one under the population census, is reflected in this column as to ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As ethnicity figures only in the document called the population census and in the ICRC, with which this document is compared, ethnicity does not figure, then the ethnicity is taken over from the population census. I don't think that Dr. Tabeau took some other ethnicity as a category, especially as she says in her methodology that she took over ethnicities from the population census.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, perhaps I briefly ask. What is new about the ethnicity? Why is it new ethnicity instead of just ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Dr. Tabeau could explain that better. I can only assume that she placed new ethnicity because there is no ethnicity as a category in the ICRC database, and she develops her information in view of ethnicity and then applies that to the data received from the ICRC.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And the column that says "matched," and yesterday you indicated the value 1 indicates that a match has been declared. What, in your opinion, is being matched?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the word "match" implies a correspondence. When you apply the method called matching, then everything depends on the criteria that you set out for the correspondence. If you want to be sure, that is to say that the degree of likelihood that the person is one and the same, then you select several elements by which the persons would correspond and for whom you can claim with a greater degree of likelihood that you have found one and the same person in two different sources. In other words, the person who is doing the matching establishes the key for it, and the key must include a certain number of elements. The more elements there are, the likelihood is closer to number 1 that two items from two different sources will correspond. The fewer the number of elements, the likelihood is smaller, and the likelihood is within the range from 0 to 1, so you can say that that the likelihood is very close to 1, and I can claim with a high degree of probability that this is one and the same person. The fewer the number of elements, you then have to make calculations. You have to review everything personally to draw some conclusions to say, yes, it is one and the same person, it could be, it may be, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can I ask one additional question. If here in this table you say the match is a 1 and not a 0, is that exclusively on the basis what you've presented here in the ICRC 2009 and in the population census, or are other elements considered by Tabeau as well when she concluded that it's a positive match?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this case, I took out examples of what Dr. Tabeau designated as matches. Now, whether she took into account others or not, there is no footnote where she would indicate what elements she took into account. But in the internal database, there is a column entitled "combinations" without an explanation of what that implies. So Dr. Tabeau could specify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the emphasis that was laid yesterday on the fact that people with the same family name, same surname, and same father's name might be different persons, and that's all we see at this moment, together with the date of birth, which is different, we do not know exactly what it was that Tabeau may conclude that this was a match? It's not visible in this table?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you identified the 2005 ICRC missing persons list as something you did not receive.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I'd like now to call up P7449 in e-court, which is Dr. Tabeau's report as to Tomasica, and I'd like to look at page 2, I believe, in both languages. And again, we need page 2 in English as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: On the Serbian at the bottom of the page, and in the English it's towards the bottom of the page from the -- I would say about two-thirds of the way down, we see a listing of sources that Dr. Tabeau says she used for the report. And under the first item, she has listed the 2009 edition of the ICRC list. If Dr. Tabeau indicates that she used the 2009 ICRC list as a source, why were you interested in the 2005 list, instead of the 2009 list?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because on the following page of the same report she says that she did everything on the basis of the census from 2005. So here she cites the source of 2009 ICRC, but on the following page she explains that it's rather not 2009 but 2005.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just to clarify something that may be a translation issue, you are recorded as saying: "Because on the following page of the same report she says that she did everything on the basis of the census from 2005." Is that what you said or was something else said?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. There is no population census from 2005. That is the ICRC list from 2005.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we could turn to the next page in both languages of Dr. Tabeau's report, and if we could focus on the second paragraph under the heading of "2.1 Missing Persons' Records of ICRC," and we see here Dr. Tabeau says: "The 2005 ICRC list of missing persons for all of Bosnia and Herzegovina used for this report was provided directly by the Geneva office of the ICRC on 17 August 2005. The data was arranged in five groups, in total 22.212 records, of which 486 were no more relevant." What you would have to say about this, based upon this selection?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Dr. Tabeau says clearly the ICRC list of missing persons from 2005 used for this report. That is to say, the report on Tomasica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And yesterday and today we've talked a little bit in passing of the integrated mortality database. I want to return to the integrated mortality database and ask you: Did you see sources identified in that database which are regularly used in demography as to the investigation of mortality?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I reviewed the database that I received and noted there were ten sources. Of those ten sources, only one is used in the official statistical research, and that's the database of births. I did not really review in detail another database that has 10.000 items, but I also didn't find there a single report from the register of births.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What are the sources that are regularly used in the field of professional academic and scientific demography as to the investigation of mortality?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The source for investigating mortality are the registers of death. For someone to be entered in the register of death, two documents need to exist. One is called a certificate of death and it's signed by a forensic doctor stating cause of death, and in most cases that happens when death occurs naturally. In violent deaths as well, but when it's known when and under what circumstances somebody died. In the situation in which we are working here, or when this is unknown, the court issues a decision and declares a person dead. The registrar may enter in the registry of death only a person for whom a certificate of death or a court decision that he is declared -- that he or she is declared dead has been issued. And therefore, documents are issued from the register of death later on about the deceased person. These are official state documents and official sources for statistics pertaining to deaths.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put one clarification question to you, Ms. Radovanovic. In your previous answer, you were referring to another database that has 10.000 items, which you didn't review in detail. Can you give a little bit more information? What kind of database is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the database on exhumed persons, which contains the exact number of the exhumed persons, from which grave they were exhumed, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Who compiled this database?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not receiving interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Then I repeat. Who compiled this database with 10.000 items?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suppose that it was compiled by Dr. Tabeau on the basis of some information that she received from certain institutions responsible for exhumations. I also suppose that the institution in question is the ICMP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That means you really don't know exactly what list you didn't review.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know exactly why I did not review it, but it only reads database on exhumed persons, and this is a type of information provided by ICMP. No databases has footnotes that would point to specific sources.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I also have a question. Madam, when you were answering the question on investigating methodology, at page 7, line 3, you said: "For someone to be entered in the register of death, two documents need to exist. One is called a certificate of death..." What is the other one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps the interpretation wasn't correct. No one can be entered in the register of deaths. According to the law, a register of deaths needs to exist. It is a state document which is kept in accordance with the Law on Registers of Deaths and Births by designated officials. The registry of deaths includes all persons who died. They are entered in it. And there is a new register for death for every year and covers the period from 1st of January to 31st of December of any given year. The registrar may only enter into this register of deaths the persons for whom a following document exists: A certificate of death signed by a forensic medical officer, or a decision of a court to the effect that the court has declared the specific person dead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Either/or, not both documents. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn back a page in Dr. Tabeau's report back to page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I'd like to look at what Dr. Tabeau has written in the middle of the third paragraph from the top that starts off with: "The fate of the victims was tracked down by pursuing the logic and chronology of the events: First the victim disappearance records were studied, to be followed by their death records. Unfortunately, among the known death cases, Tomasica victims were not reported, and thus exhumation records had to be consulted and analysed, including the victim autopsies, other post-mortem examination records of the remains, and their DNA identification. The sources on the missing exhumation identification were cross-referenced with each other, compared and analysed in an attempt to produce a reliable proof of death of the Tomasica victims. The resulting Tomasica victim list, comprising victim personal, disappearance, exhumation and identification details is attached in Annex 1 to this report. The POD list constitutes the core of the report and the reference for any conclusions drawn regarding the number [sic] of victims, their causes of death, basic demographic characteristics, and time and place of disappearance." Professor, how does this compare to what is looked at in investigating mortality in demographic scientific work? Are these sources used?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have said that the only source, the only one that's official is the registry of births and deaths; that is, the certificate of death or a court decision declaring a specific person dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we could turn to page 7 in the English in this same report, and it will be page 9 in the Serbian, and at the bottom of the page in English, and it's at the top of the page in the Serbian, Dr. Tabeau lists various records of identification and autopsy of the Bosnia and Herzegovina prosecutor's office. Are the items that are listed here, and on the next page in English but on the same page in Serbian, are these sources compatible with the sources that would be used in the scientific study of mortality in demographics?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, none of these sources is used in scientific research because they are not official sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is Dr. Tabeau, as a demographer, competent to analyse proof and cause of death according to the generally accepted principles of demography?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as it is known in demography what is a source in terms of mortality, a demographer does not try to prove anyone's death. He or she just finds and takes over the information about persons whose death has already been established. So in official scientific studies, I haven't had an occasion to see something like this. I cannot assert that that doesn't exist, but it's a fact that a demographer does not deal in establishing or proving anyone's death, even if there are documents that are available on the basis of which this can be proved, because death is proved the very moment when someone is entered in the register of deaths.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you the following. Was -- were the register of death, were they fully up to date? That means comprising most -- all or most of persons who had disappeared at the time? I mean, was it feasible to work on the basis of what you call official demography? Were those sources completely available?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it was possible to work, and Dr. Tabeau already was using the registers of deaths from Mostar. Now whether they include all persons who are assumed to be dead, I don't know. But it's a fact that persons that you can claim 100 per cent are dead and have been identified are included. It's known exactly who they are, where they are from, their dates of birth, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's be very practical. From the missing persons in Prijedor area, for how many was it formally established in the register of death that they had died when the -- well, let's say, in 2010, approximately, so well after the years of war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If all those who deceased in 2010 are recorded in the registers of death, then there is no possibility that somebody was not reported unless somebody was killed and buried and you claim that they were not. So those who are deceased, there is no reason for them not to be reported, so everything that happened in 2010 would be recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may have misunderstood my question. I was talking about missing persons. Now, I take that in 2010 there were not that many missing persons. I'm talking about those who went missing in the war years. How many of them, what percentage of those missing were officially entered in the death registers at a -- in later years? Could you tell us how many approximately, what percentage.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I cannot tell you what the percentage was. But each identified person, at the moment in time when they are identified, would you be given a certificate of death or the court would declare the person dead. That person would automatically be recorded in the register of deaths. If somebody went missing in 1992 and was identified in 2010, and if that process of identification is completed, that missing person would be recorded in the register of deaths for 2010. And then it would be precisely stated in the document on what basis the person was registered, was it on the basis of a certificate of death or a court declaration. And then would you have the day of death recorded, and there are several options here. If the date of death is in 1992, you would have the exact day, month, and year of death on the basis of statements provided by people in the process of identification. There is a different case as well: A court would declare a person dead on the basis of witnesses or some other documents, and then once again that would be recorded as that particular date of death. If somebody died in 1999 -- excuse me, 1992, and there is a document about that, they would be registered in 2010 but the date of death would be given as it was established.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And those who were not identified yet, dead bodies that were not identified, or not found, still missing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They cannot be entered in the register of deaths until you receive a certificate from the officials that the person was identified pursuant to the rules, according to the laws and regulations that apply to identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You say if you're formally registered as being dead, that's what we consider. If that has not happened, if you are not state-approved being dead, then we just ignore that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Judge Orie, I am speaking of the legal procedure and what is used in scientific research, and as for whether a demographer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just interrupt you there. I think I perfectly understood what you said, but reality may sometimes even go beyond what is legal procedure. Let's move on. I think I have understood your explanation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can look again at page 7 of Dr. Tabeau's report in the English, and it will be page 8 in the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And here Dr. Tabeau is talking about Dr. Clark. And in the second full paragraph from the top, she calls the lists of post-mortem findings from Dr. Clark as being helpful. And later on, three paragraphs down, she says that the: "... cause of death information provided by Dr. Clark has been invaluable in producing proof of death for Tomasica victims." Do you have a comment from the standpoint of the practice of demography?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I read in Dr. Clark's report, he states that the cause of death most frequently corresponds to the cause of death that were reported by his colleagues; Dr. Durmisevic and Sarajlic, I believe. He does not mention the cases when this does not correspond, but he says that most frequently they do correspond. Dr. Clark also says that he had his own definition for cause of death without explaining what that means, whereas Dr. Tabeau says that while comparing different findings on death she made corrections -- some, some corrections of these deaths.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At this trial, Dr. Tabeau testifying as a Prosecution witness testified as follows, and I'd like to read to you a portion of that testimony and then have some questions. It's from transcript page 36798, line 16, to 36799, line 7, and I'll begin the quotation: "Q. Okay. If we can move on and look at page 7 in the English and page 8 in the B/C/S. In the B/C/S, it will be the second paragraph from the bottom; and in the English, it's the second paragraph up from the subheading 2.6, and here you say, Doctor: "'Cause of death information by Dr. Clark has been invaluable in producing proof of death for Tomasica victims.' "Doctor, would have you to defer to Dr. Clark as to cause of death, or do you think there is some other source more reliable than Dr. Clark as to cause of death for these persons found in Tomasica." Dr. Tabeau's answer was as follows: "A. I think that what I said in the report, that Clark's information about causes of death is invaluable, I still stand by this statement. I also used other sources for cause of deaths as you know, because I mentioned this today. Jakarina Kosa autopsies. I also used some autopsies from 2004 and 2006 excavations in Tomasica. But, me, as a demographer and statisticians, I'm not the person to determine the cause of death, so it has to be in the hands of other specialists, pathologists; in this case, as Dr. Clark himself." And the question for you, Professor: Do you agree with what Dr. Tabeau said that as a demographer and statistician she is not the person to determine the cause of death.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in your review of Dr. Tabeau's work as to the Tomasica evidence, did Dr. Tabeau adhere to this rule that you agree with her on?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In one part of her reports she indicates that she made changes to some cause of death during computer comparisons. If she had two findings, if they did not correspond, in some places it said that it was established. I guess with Clark or somewhere else it was unestablished, that she corrected that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can look at page 24 of Dr. Tabeau's report, which we have before us in English, and it will be, I believe, page 29 in the Serbian. It will be the second paragraph up from the bottom in the Serbian, and it will be the first full paragraph at the top in the English that reads: "Last but not least, I need to explain how I dealt with the multiple CoDs available for JK victims from their associated DNA reports. For the purpose of my summary presentation of causes of death of the Tomasica victims, including those exhumed from Jakarina Kosa (see section 3.6, causes of death according to all sources jointly), I selected just one condition from every set of the associated causes. Initially, I let the computer choose one condition randomly. Then, I reviewed these choices and made the final selection. "I saw during my review that for some cases, most of the associated causes remained unascertained and just one of associated causes was well-defined. By 'well-defined,' I mean it was reported as 'gun-shot injuries of a body part'. In such cases, I corrected the computer choice of the 'unascertained' CoD and replaced it by a well-defined cause. In only a few cases I had to make a choice between injuries of two different body parts. "The logic of this approach was rooted in the purpose of this analysis. I saw my task as providing evidence about the external factors that led to the deaths or injuries of the Tomasica victims. So whenever this type of evidence came to my attention, I included it as the representation of these factors instead of leaving the answer blank ('unascertained')." Now, Professor, what Dr. Tabeau is describing here, is this something that is in accord with the generally accepted practice of scientific demography or statistics, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A demographer, first of all, does not deal with causes of death in this way, and a demographer is not competent to establish cause of death regardless of how many autopsy reports they have. Cause of death, if two forensic experts don't agree on, they either reach an agreement or call a third colleague for assistance. So a demographer does not correct the cause of death. If there are several reports in which one says unascertained and another one would refer to gunshot injuries, then it would be absurd to say that the logic of behaving in this way is the purpose of my analysis. What is the purpose of Dr. Tabeau's analysis? If I understand it correctly, it was to cause -- to prove external causes of death. Demographers can deal with those external causes of death, but that would imply the circumstances in which something occurred. And as far as the doctor is concerned, if it says a gunshot injury to the head, that would be the end-all and the be-all. As for whether it was caused during war or whether it was because somebody was killed by somebody, these are now external circumstances that could affect the outcome. So without an explanation of what the purpose of the analysis was and what was the logic applied, as far as I am concerned this is a very partial analysis. So without going into further detail, I really believe that it's really quite absurd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just ask a question, please. Madam, at page 15, lines 14, Mr. Ivetic asked you the question: "And the question for you, Professor: Do you agree with what Dr. Tabeau said that as a demographer and statistician she is not the person to determine the cause of death?" And you said you agreed with that. And then the next question was whether Dr. Tabeau stuck to that principle, and then this whole paragraph was then read to you. My question to you is do you understand this paragraph to say that Dr. Tabeau determined the cause of death, or that Dr. Tabeau was confronted with more than one possible cause of death and asked the computer to select one that was certain without her herself determining what the cause of death was? How do you understand this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand it as Dr. Tabeau establishing death. If there were several different ones and then she changed that, the instant that she made a change in the document she established it. So she established that it was no longer unascertained but it was a gun-shot injury to the head, so she established that. And when she was presenting that in her tables, she considered that to be a death, the cause of which was well defined or ascertained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So when she picks up a cause that was already written by somebody else, that's her determination. Do I understand you correctly? She -- she is not making a diagnosis. She's picking from various diagnoses. Somebody said "ascertained," another one said "not ascertained," and she picks up "ascertained." So is that her establishing the cause of death?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] She is presenting to you or to the Trial Chamber what she chose and not what exists. I am not asserting that she's changing the documents, but she is presenting what she changed and what she established. She is saying that something that was unascertained is now ascertained. She's not presenting a new document but she is changing in the tables what does not exist in the documents. If Dr. Tabeau did it professionally, she can note that and she can exclude it or she can say: If I have two options, and if we're talking about the same case, in how many cases this occurred, and what she did in this case, and what she did in another case. She should not say that the logic was the purpose of the analysis. Is the logic to present the analysis to you with the highest number of ascertained deaths? I don't know. All I know is what she wrote in the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have a short question -- oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: After this explanation, I take it that you no longer claim that she made a finding about the cause of death. She just presented a different document about an investigation by the respective persons, about the cause of death; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At no point did I say that she made a new finding. She already has two findings: One finding says unascertained, and the other one says well defined. She is changing. I don't believe -- I didn't have the opportunity to verify if she changed the first finding. But by presenting her results instead of saying that the finding is unascertained and instead of calculating that, she changes that and she says: I have decided to present to the Trial Chamber that that was changed. I cannot believe that she would made -- make any changes to the finding in the original documents, but she changes that by presenting the cause of death in her tables and by presenting to you that all causes of death were ascertained even though they were not; namely, in cases where the option was either yes or no, she changed them to a "yes." I really didn't have enough time to look at each of those documents to say: Well, look, for this and this person, this pathologist says this, and the second pathologist says that. I don't believe that Dr. Tabeau changed documents written by a pathologist, but she concluded: I have two findings. This one says unascertained, this one arrived later as ascertained, so I'm going to use the one that's ascertained and I'm going to present that in my tables as an ascertained cause of death. I believe that that is not professionally correct. Even in cases such as this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you for this long explanation again. Now you made it quite clear what you are presenting here in the courtroom. At the beginning, you said Dr. Tabeau says that while comparing different findings, she made corrections. Some corrections of these deaths. What I -- what you now told us is not correction of death but choosing a document which she finds more reliable and with more details. This is what I now understand from your testimony; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dr. Tabeau does not say that. She said: I changed the cause of death. I just assume that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You said that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes -- no. But you can read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, I have to interrupt you. You said that she changed the cause of death. But let us continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one other question. Dr. Tabeau describes situations where the causes of death are not fully consistent, that she asked the computer to make a random choice, and that she later then in a few cases has corrected that random choice because she thought there was a good reason to choose for either of the options. Could you tell us, approximately, have you verified, and how many cases, because she describes this as a rather rare situation where she made such corrections, do you have any idea about the quantity of those cases and how they impact on the statistics, what -- what changes it causes in the statistical analysis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have an idea but Dr. Tabeau should have stated that. That would have been professional. She changed it via the computer. She should have said 10, 15, or 20. My idea is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question was not whether she should have done it differently. That is clear from your explanation. You have, as you say -- you have an idea about that. Could you tell us what that idea is, and then talking in terms of quantity.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My idea is that if you conceal a piece of data like that, it's probably not something that is just small. I'm not saying that I'm right. But as for whether it was minimal, what does it mean in a number of cases? She could have said it was in 0.2 per cent or 0.3 per cent of cases. I was not able to do that. I didn't have enough time. But my idea is that if the demographer and statistician does not present that, as a demographer you have a reason probably for omitting this particular data.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you want to conceal something, would you openly explain what you did?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in order to be able to say -- but, yes, I did cite that in a number of cases. But if it's a number of cases, then can you please express it in the way that an expert, a professional, would express it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, my question was whether if you want to conceal something, whether you would openly explain what you did.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You and I don't agree that this is an open explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I -- I believe that this is not an open explanation. This is an expert here who cannot just say in a number of. Why didn't she put three in parentheses, for example, or one? Our profession asks us to present things in an exact way with numbers, so this number of several or a few causes me to doubt things. I don't know if it's a lot or just a few. But I am setting out from the fact that if you are an expert and you say a number, then you open parentheses and you say three, seven cases, one, and this is what is causing me to doubt it because if you're a professional you know how a statistician or a demographer would express themselves: By using numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You're questioning her integrity.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that she is not professionally correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that wasn't my question. My question was whether you are questioning her integrity, which is more than not acting professionally but intentionally doing so to hide something. That's what are you saying Dr. Tabeau has done.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If that is how we define integrity, then yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed -- oh, no, I'm looking at the clock. I think I should advise you not to proceed at this moment, Mr. Ivetic. Professor Radovanovic, we'll take a break and we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're waiting for the witness to be escorted in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Professor, can you tell us in the generally accepted practice of scientific demography, how are violent deaths categorised?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Violent deaths caused by murder, accident, or suicide.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, at our trial Dr. Tabeau testified as follows at transcript page 36855, line 21, to 36856, line 9: "Q. Okay. Now, would you agree with me that in the fields of statistics and demography, violent death is categorised into three category: Accidental death, suicide, and homicide? "A. Yes. Broadly speaking, yes. "Q. And would you agree homicide is further subdivided into justifiable homicide and murder? "A. Yes. "Q. Now when you conclude in your report that all Tomasica victims died violent deaths, can you differentiate between accidental death, suicide, and the two forms of homicide, or are all these forms of violent death included in your finding? "A. Of course, I couldn't differentiate as my knowledge of the circumstances was not enough to make these kind of divides or categorisations." Professor, what would be your comment as to Dr. Tabeau's testimony?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau perhaps could not distribute them exactly according to circumstances and show how these persons lost their lives, but it would have been professionally correct if she had at least hinted that within all these deaths may be also the deaths that were -- that occurred in combat. Whether she was able to divide between the two, I don't think so. Probably not because there is not sufficient information. But there are documents available that confirm that some persons did lose their lives in combat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just ask a question. How would you delineate a person who has died in combat, ma'am, as a demographer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is a violent death which is not a result of execution but which occurred in combat, which is greatly different from execution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How do you come to that conclusion when you are looking at a body that is dead already with bullets in it? How do you conclude that these bullets were fired in combat and not in execution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are documents saying that on a specific date there was combat under way and that some persons were killed in combat. There is also a report by a French policeman who says that persons whose first and last names are known and who were members of Territorial Defence were excluded because they perished in combat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And it would not be a professional determination in demography or which -- you're quoting other sources that tell us how the person died? Can she make a professional determination as a demographer that a person died in combat or not? That's my question, not whether she can -- she uses other sources.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if she has documents saying so, then she may indicate that not all deaths that she presents occurred outside combat or if she could indicate that they occurred in and out of combat, because as it is it's insinuated that all the deaths presented by Dr. Tabeau were caused by execution or ethnic cleansing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Does she say they were caused by execution or does she say they were caused violently? Let's just be clear what she says.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] She says that all the deaths were -- that all deaths occurred under identical circumstances due to an ethnic cleansing campaign, and it is a fact that all deaths did not occur under identical circumstances because there are documents showing that the circumstances were not identical; that is to say, which confirm that there was combat too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We have now moved away from the question I was asking. The question I was asking is how you distinguish death by execution from death by -- in combat where people -- where the description is just violent deaths and how you make that distinction professionally as a demographer. You have given your answer. Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Ivetic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would have -- nevertheless, have one question. Ms. Radovanovic, you're saying there are documents which says there were combat, and I consider that important for this Court. Would that allow to distinguish between those who died in combat or those who died as from execution? I mean, the fact that there was combat, would that be sufficient to enable someone to determine that the persons died in combat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Depends on what a document you consult. If, for example, there is a list from the BiH army, the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and if the list mentions soldiers who died, you can then take the data, and I cannot claim that some of them died in combat and some not, but it's a fact that they are soldiers, not civilians. And it's only in 2009 that Dr. Tabeau says in Srebrenica 70 per cent were soldiers. Up until 2009 they were all treated, and it was suggested, that they were all civilians. So it's one of the documents where you can distinguish troops from civilians. Another -- or, rather, other documents are individual documents. I've stated some of them. And these documents mention that fighting occurred on a specific date, at a specific place, and that there were casualties. Now, Dr. Tabeau perhaps may not individually state who was killed in combat and who was not, but she could say that possibly some of the deaths occurred in combat. As, for example, Nicolas Sebire does in his report. I'm not sure if I am pronouncing his name right. He even says that there is a database including issue -- decisions issued by court declaring those persons dead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the question still is, I think, what is within the competence of demographers and what is within the competence of a court which is to combine all the information to come to conclusions. But let's leave it to that. I have heard your explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Again, I have a follow-up question because all this was triggered by one sentence, that's on page 24, lines 21 to 23. You said, I quote: "But there are documents available that confirm that some persons did lose their lives in combat." How many persons and on the basis of which documents did you say that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my report, I note which documents I have in mind, but I don't know how many persons. Dr. Tabeau would have been professionally correct if she had at least suggested the possibility that some of those that she lists as those who died and who were victims of Tomasica may have died in combat. She could have suggested the same thing for Srebrenica. But up until 2009, not a single word to that effect was ever uttered and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I am asking you. And we are dealing here with Tomasica, not with Srebrenica. How many? If you say there are documents available that some persons did lose their lives in combat, how many and on the basis of which documents? If you don't know, then we can proceed, but please answer this question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The documents which I listed. I can't tell you off the top of my head, but it's mentioned in those documents that on such and such a day there was combat in such and such a place. If Dr. Tabeau draws conclusions at the end of her report about incidents per day, in accordance with the indictment against General Mladic, then on the basis of these incidents, dates, and places, she could have concluded that some combat took place as well. She perhaps couldn't have said this specific person died in combat or not and this one didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You didn't answer my question, but let's continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, excuse me, I really wish to answer your question. But perhaps I don't understand. If the question is whether it's possible to distinguish who exactly died in combat and who didn't, then it's no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Ms. Radovanovic, I quoted a sentence you said earlier, and I wanted to know the background of that, and you were not able to give me the background. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I have misunderstood you then.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't know if translation is an issue, but in paragraph 7 of Professor Radovanovic she says there are documents confirming that victims could have also died, and in -- apart from that one section Your Honour has read, every other answer she has given today, that I've paid attention to, has talked about possibilities and not actualities. And unfortunately I did not listen to the B/C/S of that one part that was cited to or missed, whether it was "could" or "could have." But I do want to point out that the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That can you verified, as you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I know, I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there is any reason to have the interpretation verified, we'll do that in order to avoid whatever misunderstandings, Mr. Ivetic, and you know that. Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can then turn to 1D6184 in e-court, and that will be Professor Radovanovic's report. And just for the record, the paragraph 7 that I mentioned is on page 6 in English and page 6 in Serbian. But I'd like to turn to page 11 in English and page 13 in Serbian and paragraph 25 of Professor Radovanovic's report. I don't know if everyone else is looking at a black screen or if it's just me, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, we don't have anything on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's saving power.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we find something on our screens now, so we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. If we can now then have the English version, which is to be found on page number 11, and it will be paragraph 25 of the report, that reads: "The fact that sources containing court rulings of death existing in the Demographic Unit have been discarded without any explanation having been given" --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, I cannot follow. That's which paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 25.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: "The fact that sources containing court rulings of death existing in the Demographic Unit" --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Apparently the English is bleeding through on the B/C/S channel, at least on this side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then let's restart. If you slowly read again and I'll follow on the B/C/S channel whether that gives, indeed, B/C/S interpretation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: "The fact that sources containing court rulings of death existing in the Demographic Unit have been discarded without any explanation having been given for not using them in the Report of 20 August 2014, gives rise to reasonable suspicion that these documents are being ignored in a calculated manner. Perhaps because in the decisions of some courts it is stated 'some individuals were last seen while they were involved in the local Territorial Defence (TO). As it is possible that they died in the course of combat activities, they were not taken into consideration, except when other evidence indicates that they were captured and/or detained by the opponent forces and later killed.' Thus, it was possible at least to suggest, if not precisely establish, ... that not all victims had died under the same circumstances, i.e., had been executed, as the expert witness insinuates. Apart from that, an account should be taken of the fact that the expert witness, announcing problems in establishing military versus civilian status, observes that it 'can be seen differently, depending on circumstances of death. A soldier shot dead when he/she was not participating in combat (e.g. while on leave) must be seen as a civilian. And a civilian shot in fighting in which he/she used a gun and thus was engaged in combat would be a combatant' why does the expert witness 'overlook' the possibility that there had been both soldiers and combatants among the victims of Tomasica and Prijedor generally?" Is this the section that you earlier identified as talking about reports that were in the Demographic Unit that talks about combat and the possibility that certain individuals may have been deceased in combat?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Here one of the items you reference in the footnotes is a 2002 report of Prosecution Investigator Nicolas Sebire. Given that the Prosecution's Office has this information, dated 2002, precisely as to Prijedor, as to persons last seen in the TO that possibly died in combat, would a demographer following generally accepted scientific methodology consider such a report relevant to investigating the death of persons from Tomasica in Prijedor to determine how they may have died?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic which footnote were you referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That would be footnote number 16, I believe. Let me just turn to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was 15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It should be 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: 15, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that in evidence, for us? Just for us to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It is not. It is on our list. We could -- I could get you the number of that. I don't have the list in front of me right now, but it is uploaded, I believe, in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I just wondered whether we have that available.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are excerpts of this document already in evidence upped P3282, and the entire document is 65 ter 26260.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then you consider, I don't know how long the document is, what we would need and what would assist us in evaluating this. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you list several other documents in footnote number 17 that you say show that there was armed conflict in certain areas. Would you have expected Dr. Tabeau, if following a generally accepted professional scientific methodology, to have looked at such information contained in such documents?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It would have been correct on her side to study them. She may have noted why she wouldn't use them, but she shouldn't pretend as if they did not exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can go to the next page in the Serbian, and it will be the same page of your report in the English --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before you do that, may I ask for a clarification. Mr. Ivetic, when you started this line of questioning, you were referring to paragraph 7 on page 6 in the English and page 6 in Serbian. There, I read, in paragraph 7: "The expert witness insinuates but does not prove that all victims were executed although there exist documents confirming that the victims could also have died in combat." This is in paragraph 7 of the witness's report. I would like to know from Ms. Radovanovic, now we heard about the report of Mr. Nicolas Sebire of 2002. Is that the only report you are referring to here, the only document, or have you anything else in mind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This paragraph 7 is a summary so it's shortened, and it's not the only one. This refers also to other documents under footnote 17 from paragraph 25. As this is a summary, I did not write about it expansively. I did in further text. But this is just a conclusion drawn from what follows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. But in footnote 17 we have only a list of documents with ERN numbers. Can you summarise what kind of documents are these? There are no titles, and we have no idea what kind of documents these are.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I cannot remember exactly how they are called, but those are mostly reports -- I have them in my room, so if you like I can bring them. Reports submitted by certain persons about what happened on a specific day, where there was combat, and so on and so forth. I can't remember who it was that submitted them, but I can look, I have them in my bag in my room, and tell you exactly what documents these are. These are some kinds of minutes that were then sent with reports on what was going on, on specific dates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Do you have any information if one or more of these victims of combat mentioned in these documents ended up in the Tomasica mass grave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I did not examine this. I took it more as an example that there was combat on specific dates and in specific places.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now looking at paragraph number 26, and here you deal with Dr. Tabeau's reference to machine-gun fire. For a demographer, does one ever deal with whether someone is killed by a gun, machine-gun, or by other means; and, if so, when?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they deal with causes of death that were given by forensic specialists. They can say a gun-shot wound to the head, but whether it's from a machine-gun or a pistol or something would have nothing to do with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now if I could ask you about something that Dr. Tabeau testified about during our trial, and that was at transcript page 36800, lines 8 through 20. I will read as follows when I asked her about the testimony of Dr. Clark, and it went like this: "Q. I would like to put one last question regarding this topic by way of a conclusion. "Is it correct that, as a scientist, you cannot exclude the possibility that any or some of the people were killed in combat? "A. Yes, I can't -- I can't exclude that." And that's citing now Dr. Clark. And then I asked Dr. Tabeau about this testimony of Dr. Clark as follows: "Is this finding by Dr. Clark highly consistent with your results in doing your work as to the bodies recovered from Tomasica? "A. Sir, I didn't any -- I didn't study any sources based on which I could say that someone died in combat or in non-combat situation. I actually draw no conclusions about that. So whatever Mr. Clark said in his testimony, it is his opinion, but I cannot make any statements at this moment on that." And that's the end of the citation. Professor, what would be your comments as to this testimony.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau said it well, that she did not look at any other sources that would indicate something else, and Dr. Clark presents the causes of death. I do not recall Dr. Clark writing that anybody died from machine-gun fire. I don't think there's anything like that in his reports. But he does talk about pistol shots, how many shots, and so on and so forth, but for a demographer that would not be something of significance. Even Dr. Clark, if I recall, does not rule out the possibility that some persons were killed in combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In the continuation of her testimony on this topic, Dr. Tabeau at transcript page 36810, lines 9 through 14, testified as follows: "Q. Dr. Tabeau, do you think differentiating between combat-related deaths and those from ethnic cleansing is irrelevant for purposes of your report? "A. I never said it is irrelevant for the purposes of my report, but I was just not able to study sources that would be telling me about the combat and non-combat incidents." Professor, what would be your comment as to this part of the testimony.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would ask why Dr. Tabeau did not have that opportunity. She has a database that she formed herself with her associates. I assume that she knows the content of the database. If she did not have the opportunity, she should have given a reason; perhaps lack of time, lack of available material. The fact that she did not have the opportunity to do something does not mean that that particular thing does not exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did Dr. Tabeau have access at the Demographic Unit to other sources of army documents listing casualties, apart from the Nicolas Sebire report that you cited to in your report.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Demographic Unit has everything that Dr. Tabeau and her assistants created, meaning different databases based on the special project that she was heading at the Office of the Prosecutor. She knows everything that those databases contain, and she knows which documents are available. If I was able to receive some things from the Defence, I don't think that the Defence found them on the street. These documents were recorded, registered if they refer to the population. I mean, I assume that Dr. Tabeau had these same documents as well. I don't know everything that is contained in the database -- in the databases of the Demographic Unit because I never had access to the overall data of the Demographic Unit. I am not aware of any catalogue existing which would say we have these documents at our disposal, so that I would be able to go through that list and say: Well, this would be interesting to me. The demographic database familiarity with it and its contents is something that is known to Dr. Tabeau, so she can make a selection. I'm not able to make a selection. I can rely on what she refers to in her report. I can ask for that. Also, things that I get. If the lawyers help me, they find a report; for example, I received Nicolas Sebire's report in The Hague. I did not know about that report earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I try to get a focused comment on the following matter. What Dr. Tabeau says, as quoted, is that she was unable to distinguish between combat-related death and death from ethnic cleansing because she was not able to study sources that would be telling her about the combat and non-combat incidents. Now, you are saying: You should have told us I have no time, et cetera. Are you aware - and I really would be interested in it - are you aware of sources which clearly distinguish between incidents as a result of combat and incidents which are considered to be part of ethnic cleansing? Because we -- over the last hour, we discussed in quite some detail that whereas almost everyone concedes that people may have died in combat, and there may have been combat, but it's very difficult to specifically identify this was a combat victim and this was an ethnic cleansing victim. So where you say she should have explained that she had no time, but she should have done it, or explained why she didn't do it, here, at least as I understand it, she says: I didn't have such sources. My question for you, therefore, is: Are you aware of sources which identify clearly between this incident is a combat victim and that incident is an ethnic cleansing victim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have such information, but I think that the Demographic Unit at least has parts or sections --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. Ms. Tabeau says, I don't have such sources. You're saying, I'm not aware of such sources but she must have them. Could you tell us why you conclude that where she says, I have no such sources, what makes you believe - and I really would be interested to know - what makes you believe that she did have such sources?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] She does not say that she does not have them. She just says that she did not study them. At least that's what I got in the translation that I had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Then let me read it exactly. "I was just not able to study sources that would be telling me about the combat and non-combat incidents." You apparently understood this as such sources do exist, but I was unable - lack of time, whatever it would be - and you have not considered this possibly to be understood as I wasn't able because they do not exist.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If she did not have these sources, at least this is my reasoning, the doctor would say, I do not have sources on the basis of which I could make that conclusion. If she does say I was not able to study, then these sources do exist, or at least a part of such sources exists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But that's your linguistic analysis of the answer. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could look at paragraph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have a question in respect of paragraph 26. Ms. Radovanovic, you say in paragraphs 26 that: For Dr. Tabeau to say that shooting was from machine-gun, machine -- or sometimes handguns is intellectually dishonest if account is not taken of the fact that there had also been combatants amongst the dead. My question is: Is it your position that combatants would not be killed by machine-guns or handguns.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can't say it if you have data anywhere that there was fire from a machine-gun or machine-guns. Based on the sources cited by Dr. Tabeau, and then during questioning, she says that this is something she saw at John Clark's reports and then this is missing in the -- in the analysis of John Clark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm going to interrupt you because you're not answering my question at all. My question is: Is it your position that combatants cannot be killed with machine or sometimes handguns because you're saying by alleging that people were killed with machine or sometimes handguns is intellectually dishonest because it does not take account of the fact that others were combatants. My question to you is are saying combatants cannot be killed with machine or handguns.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, if you're asking for the conclusion of the witness, you have to read the full conclusion, which after the comma says: "... as well as that not a single document that the expert witness uses contains information about machine-gun fire." That's the finding in that paragraph, so you can't take one part of it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I think you wanted to make a suggestion, a brief suggestion to Judge Moloto.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's not the language you used. You told him what he had to do, yes? Okay, therefore I leave it in the hands of Judge Moloto again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But next time you may suggest but not tell Judge Moloto what he should have done, whether it's right or wrong what you're telling, but that's not the way we address one of my colleagues. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I am aware of the rest of that sentence, and the rest of that sentence really doesn't turn around the question I'm asking. The fact that there is not a single document that the expert witness uses contains information about machine-guns, it's -- should then -- the -- the expert should be challenged on the basis that she has -- doesn't give us a source of where she get the information that machine-guns were used. I'm dealing with a question of where she is being accused of being intellectually dishonest simply because she uses -- she says the bodies were shot at with machine or sometimes handguns. Now if you -- and my question is: Is it the position of this expert that combatants are not shot at -- cannot be shot at with machine or sometimes hand guns? That's all I'm asking. It has nothing to do with the rest of the sentence. And, Madam Radovanovic, will you please answer my question, if you can? And I just want to say I take a strong exception to your comments.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Combatants can be shot at with anything, machine-guns, rockets, bombs. If this is what you're asking me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and if Dr. Tabeau concluded that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But this is what you're concluding. You're concluding that because she says machine-guns and guns were used, therefore, she is excluding combatants. Now you're saying that combatants can also be shot at with machine-guns, which in fact then contradicts what you are saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours I would have to object to the question as posed and give Your Honours some instruction as advice that the conclusion, as stated in the report, contains additional matters which you have not raised which go towards the conclusion. So to say and to pull out one half of the conclusion and say your conclusion is based on A while ignoring part B, which is also part of the conclusion, I believe is creating a false record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is the implicit suggestion which was dealt with by Judge Moloto, and you may now proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, let's turn to paragraph 24 of the report, on page 10 in English at the bottom, and it will be page 13 in Serbian, and here we can see what Dr. Tabeau said about her access to other documents. Here you are citing Dr. Tabeau's article from 2005 that says: "Only a few sources can be taken as safe and sound, for instance, records from" --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I think we have to turn the page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: "... death certificates, court decisions proclaiming persons dead, and death records of armed forces from the archives of the Ministry of Defence." Has Dr. Tabeau utilized death records from the archives in the Ministry of Defence in other reports that you have reviewed?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, she did not use these documents anywhere in the reports that I reviewed. Except in 2009, the Ministry of Defence, in Srebrenica, so only in 2009, but can I also say that it's not actually an official document. I can agree with Dr. Tabeau that she included it in the -- as an official document, but in scientific work it's not counted as an official document. An official document would only be the certificate of death or a court decision to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we return to paragraph 25 of your report, we have another citation, I believe, from the same 2005 article of Dr. Tabeau. I read it before, so I won't read it again, but it is in relation to footnote number 18 in paragraph 25 of your report. Can you reconcile with what Dr. Tabeau has written in 2005 and what she has not done in Tomasica?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If Dr. Tabeau knows what the documents are that are certain and valid and if she informs the expert public about that, then I think that it would have been professionally correct for her to also inform the Trial Chamber and to say: These are documents that are used in scientific expert studies, but I'm not using that, I'm using something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, on the same topic at transcript page 36810, lines 15 through 20, Dr. Tabeau testified as follows: "Q. Given that you concede combat is also a violent death, different than people killed as non-combatants or killed not in combat, will you agree that there exists a possibility that some or all Tomasica bodies may equally be from combat as they may be from what you've called ethnic cleansing? "A. I cannot exclude this option." What comment do you have on this testimony of Dr. Tabeau in relation to her expert report as to Tomasica.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She did not write that anywhere in her report. Quite to the contrary. She concludes that all of that is a consequence of ethnic cleansing, and a widespread campaign of ethnic cleansing at that. Nowhere does she indicate the possibility that this could have been in different circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can look at Dr. Tabeau's report, it will be P7449 in e-court. It will be page 47 in the English and page 60 in the B/C/S. And it will be under the heading "Conclusions," which appears two pages prior, so that's the section of the report we're dealing with. And it will be the last paragraph in the report before the listing of annexes to the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We're still waiting for the Serbian. If I can assist, it's page 60 in the Serbian. And it's at the very bottom of the page in the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And here Dr. Tabeau, as the very last thing she writes in her report, says: "All in all, a significant evidence was presented in this report which supports the conclusion that all Tomasica victims died violent deaths in extremely dramatic circumstances of a broader campaign of ethnic cleansing in the Prijedor municipality and as part of the ARK ethnic cleansing campaign." First of all, how do you understand this? Is this a conclusion of Dr. Tabeau or something else?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's Dr. Tabeau's final conclusion. It's in the section entitled "Conclusion" as the final point of the overall conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can now take a look at 1D6184 again, that would be your report, and paragraph 31 of the same, which is found on page 13 in the English, page 16 in the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you a question. You said this is Dr. Tabeau's conclusion. What is her conclusion, that there is evidence which supports; or is it her conclusion that this is what happened, that all Tomasica victims died violent death in extremely dramatic circumstances, et cetera? What is her conclusion, that there is significant evidence to support that or that this is what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Her conclusion is that there is evidence but that it happened in a ethnic cleansing campaign in extremely dramatic circumstances. I accept the number of the dead from Tomasica. I'm not going to dispute the number or the fact that they are dead. I am just asking: What led her to conclude that it was a consequence of a broader campaign of ethnic cleansing in extremely dramatic circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me try to again explain to you what my problem is. My problem is that Dr. Tabeau points at the existence of what she calls significant evidence that something may have happened. She doesn't say that's what happened, but she says there's significant evidence that supports that it has happened, which I understand - but please correct me when you read it in a different way - that she does not draw that final conclusion, although she points at the significance of the evidence which would support such a conclusion. That's the reason why I'm asking you. Because the question put to you by Mr. Ivetic was: Is this here conclusion. And therefore, I asked you: Is her conclusion that significant evidence exists where she refrains from saying that it's what happened, or is it her conclusion that this is what happened.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] She says that that is what really happened and that Tomasica corroborates the widespread campaign; namely, that that really happened and that that is evidence of a broader campaign of ethnic cleansing. That is how I understand this conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's how you read the conclusion which was quoted. That's your linguistical analysis of the lines that were read to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, Judge Orie. I am reading what Dr. Tabeau wrote, and what the attorney read to me as a direct quote of what Dr. Tabeau wrote --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- let's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- in the last lines of her conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's how you interpret what was read to you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think we're at the time for the break again, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's time for a break, indeed. Professor Radovanovic, we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll resume at 20 minutes past midday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll briefly move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Lukic, would you remind your client that he's supposed not to speak aloud.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I had wanted to ask about paragraph 31 of your report where you say that Dr. Tabeau has stepped outside her profession for the purposes of the analysis and that is obviously biased in selecting sources of data. In this regard, I'd like to -- first of all, do you stand by paragraph 31 of your report, as written?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to address the use of the term "ethnic cleansing" by Dr. Tabeau since the Trial Chamber had several questions about it in the last session. I'd like to present to you various testimony of Dr. Tabeau precisely on the use of the term "ethnic cleansing," and I'll take each of the sections of her testimony one by one and then ask for comments as to each. So the entire section of the transcript that I will be talking about is from transcript page 36802, line 18, through 36804, line 12. The first part of the testimony is as follows: "Q. Then do you feel that your conclusions as to ethnic cleansing are complete since you did not take into account the potential impact or role of combat as to the bodies recovered from Tomasica?" And the answer of Dr. Tabeau was as follows: "A. I think that the report I made is not about the ethnic cleansing in the first place. It is about the victims from Tomasica in the first place --" And then in the continuation of the transcript, the second question was asked: "Q. Doctor, I beg to differ. The conclusion I just read is the penultimate conclusion of your report. I put it to you that it is the basis of your report and it is the key part of your report. If you do not want us to rely upon that conclusion, please say so." And Dr. Tabeau's answer was: "Well, to me I see a clear picture of ethnic cleansing based on the records I studied, based on the records of missing persons, from the Prijedor municipality - in particular from the Prijedor municipality and from the ARK area as such. The fact that many victims went missing on a few days in July, the 20th, 23, 4th, and 5th, these are huge numbers." Professor, what comment do you have as to Dr. Tabeau's testimony on this matter.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, it is contradictory.
